newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE flaxseed closes higher, canola drifts lower.
newsitem.headline: WCE flaxseed closes higher, canola drifts lower.

text.p: WCE flaxseed futures closed higher boosted by commercial buying while canola was dragged to lower closes by weakness in CBOT soybeans, traders said.
"It (flax) is tight. I'm hearing somebody needs flax before Thunder Bay freezes up," one WCE oilseed trader said.

Active two-way commercial trade was noted in canola. Buying by domestic crushers underpinned values although there continued to be concern that canola was still too highly priced to be competitive in the oilseed market.
November flax closed $1.50 higher at $368.50 per tonne while November canola ended $1.80 loer at $394.00.
Western barley futures closed higher boosted by commission house short covering although a pick up in the pace of hedge sales eroded gains late.

Traders said the rally was largely technically based with the market's improved performance during the last few days inspiring a much more constructive chart outlook. Prices sunk to a 15-month low earlier this month.

Commission house short covering was also a feature in feed wheat. December wheat closed $1.20 higher at $168.50 with November barley up $1.00 at $141.00. December oats ended off $0.90 at $121.00. Feed peas were tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats).
